label: First two copy steps when orig token 1 or 2 is from a preferred set (3, 2, o, p, g, l, h, ...)
explanation: Early-copy-phase feature: 99% of mass is in the copy phase, about 89% at recall_idx 1-2 (the steps right after <DEL> where the model echoes orig(0) and outputs orig(1), then orig(2)), with a tail at recall_idx 3. It almost never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter step. Magnitude depends on which tokens are being recalled next: it is strongest when orig(1)/orig(2) are 3 (lift 6x), then o, 2, p, g, l, h. The top examples are all sequences starting X 3 3 ..., where it hits about 0.9 of max at recall 1 and about 0.6 at recall 2. Position alone (recall_idx<=2) gets F1 0.53 with mass recall 0.89. Adding the token-identity condition raises F1 to about 0.61, but the token dependence is graded rather than a clean set, so precision stays incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: 3, o, 2, p, g, h; least: y, n, s, w) and the next token to output (most: 3, p, o, 2, h, g; least: y, n, s, w); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, recall_idx=1, t=4.
